location: Boundaries > Always (Slots bullet: '--cleanup-orphans once before the first admission, every mode'); Tasks > docs (headless.md: 'automatic --cleanup-orphans before wait-slots')
issue: The spec says when the automatic cleanup runs in two different ways, and one of them contradicts the contract. The Slots bullet runs it once before the first admission of every run. cell-contract.md > Config keys and SPEC Constraints run it 'before entering wait-slots', so only when the cap is actually full. The docs task copies the contract wording, so the docs would describe different behaviour from the code. The spec also never says whether cleanup results (removed/skipped/errors) are logged, printed or recorded anywhere, even though this is the one destructive action headless runs now take on jobs they did not start.
implementation_impact: An implementer must pick one trigger. Running it on every invocation adds a full container+network listing and inspect pass (up to DOCKER_CMD_TIMEOUT per call) to every single-cell canary run. Running it only before wait-slots contradicts the frozen spec text. Whichever is picked, a test or a docs sentence will be wrong, and container removals happen silently.
suggestion: State one trigger that matches the contract: once per run, the first time an admission attempt fails, before the first START wait-slots line. Require the cleanup result's removed/skipped/errors lists to go to stderr and to the waiting version's progress log, and say that a 'partial' cleanup status does not abort the run.

location: Design Notes > Claims; Tasks > ps-flashlight-run.py (`daemon_slot_usage()` -> (used, counted list, ok))
issue: A claim counts only while no running container carries its psm.run. But daemon_slot_usage returns only the summed slots, a 'psm.job@host=cost' list and an ok flag. It does not return the psm.run labels of the counted containers. The admission code therefore cannot decide from the same snapshot whether a claim is already represented by a running container. A second docker query, or registry reads done at a different time, opens a window where a container starts between the two reads. That container is then counted neither as a label nor as a claim (under-count, so over-admission past the host cap), or it is counted twice.
implementation_impact: The cap can be exceeded under exactly the concurrency CAP-3 is meant to control. The stubbed test harness cannot express the claim-vs-container interaction at all, so AC2 and any 'claim stops counting once its container runs' test cannot be written against the specified signature.
suggestion: Make daemon_slot_usage return the per-container (psm.run, psm.job, owner host, cost) tuples from one `docker ps --format` call. Specify the order under slots.lock: read the registry claims first, then take one docker snapshot, then discount the claims whose run appears in that snapshot. Add a test where a claim's run appears in the stubbed snapshot and is counted exactly once.

location: Boundaries > Always (Slots: 'startup-timeout clock counts only while none of this run's own children is in flight; timeout -> no-slots for every still-queued cell')
issue: The spec turns the contract's per-cell wait bound (cell-contract.md > Config keys: 'the cell waits ... for at most the startup timeout') into one run-level clock that expires every still-queued cell at once. It does not say whether that clock accumulates across separate gaps (cell 2 waits 100 s in one gap, cell 3 waits 100 s in a later gap, so the total of 200 s exceeds 180 s), or whether it resets when a cell is admitted. This deviation from the contract is not listed under Ask First or Design Notes.
implementation_impact: Depending on the reading, a cell that personally waited well under the timeout can be reported no-slots. Two cells of a run would then become an infra cause that later feeds CAP-1's blocked-infra rule. Tests for the 'Own queue' and 'Foreign full' rows can pass under either reading, so the ambiguity survives review.
suggestion: Define the clock per queued cell, starting when that cell first fails admission and pausing while any own child is in flight. Alternatively, keep one run clock but state that it resets on every admission and record it as a deliberate interim decision. Add an I/O row with two separated foreign-full gaps that each stay under the timeout.

location: Boundaries > Always (Fail-fast bullet) and Design Notes > Trigger
issue: The spec changes the contract trigger from 'the first child that exits 3' (cell-contract.md > Runner > Fail-fast) to 'an appended fail record', and justifies the change in Design Notes. Its own Ask First section says that changing a contract rule needs approval, and the spec neither flags this change as approved nor adds it to the contract. It also leaves three cases open. (a) Two children reaped in the same wait() batch: the existing run_children sorts a batch by plan order, not completion order, so the cell named in 'fail-fast after <ver>:<browser>' is decided by plan order. (b) A fail record that was appended and is followed by a child exit 2 from an in-flight child: which reason do the queued cells get? (c) Are not-run records written at trigger time or after in-flight children finish?
implementation_impact: Reviewers checking the code against cell-contract.md will flag the trigger as a defect. The not-run reason string (fail-fast vs input-error) and the record order in `appended` are nondeterministic between implementations, and tests asserting the reason text are fragile.
suggestion: Either get the trigger change approved and write it back into cell-contract.md > Runner, or follow the contract. State that the first trigger wins and fixes the reason. State that not-run records for still-queued cells are appended immediately at the trigger, before in-flight children are reaped. State that ties inside one reap batch follow plan order (and document that 'completion order' is approximate there).

location: Boundaries > Always (Honesty law: 'run exit 3 if any fail, else 1 if any record not pass') vs Fail-fast bullet ('still exits 2') and contract Runner > Output (skipped -> exit 0)
issue: The exit-code sentence is incomplete and contradicts the other rules. It omits the precedence of exit 2 (child exit 2, which the previous slice ranks above fail), of 143 (stop), and of the 'skipped' path, which exits 0 even when no-slots or not-run records were appended in the same run. Read literally, 'else 1 if any record not pass' forbids exit 0 for a run that appended no-slots records and had one skipped child, but the contract requires exit 0 with `skipped` there.
implementation_impact: An implementer following this spec alone writes an exit ladder that differs from the existing run_e2e ladder and the contract, and the existing tests for skipped and exit 2 either break or are 'fixed' in the wrong direction.
suggestion: Replace the sentence with the full ordered ladder: 143 stopped; 2 append error (no line) or child exit 2 (line `ran`); 3 any appended fail; 0 + `skipped` when a child skipped and no fail; 1 when any appended record is not pass (including not-run and no-slots) or nothing was appended; else 0. Add a matrix row with a skipped child plus a no-slots record.

location: Design Notes > Records without a child; contract Phase timings (ps-run-layer truncates the version's progress log before wait-slots)
issue: Truncation is defined only for a version that enters wait-slots ('wait-slots is recorded only when the first admission attempt failed') and for a never-started version (one DONE line). The spec does not say whether ps-run-layer truncates the log of a version admitted on its first attempt. Every child now gets --progress-append, so if nothing truncates that log, it keeps the previous run's lines, including an old DONE and old bring-up lines. That breaks the AC 'no bring-up' style assertions and the stall rule. The spec also does not say what DONE line ps-run-layer writes for a version still in wait-slots when the run is stopped (exit 143), crashes, or hits an append error. With no DONE, the run-phases.md stall rule (no line for about 3 minutes and no DONE = hung) flags those logs forever.
implementation_impact: Stale lines from earlier runs leak into logs read as current, which is the problem contract Phase timings exists to prevent. Orchestrators following the stall rule report phantom hangs after every stopped run.
suggestion: Require ps-run-layer to truncate every queued version's log at run start, before cleanup and admission, whether or not it later waits. Require a DONE line (`rc=stopped`, `rc=crash`, `rc=append-error`) on every exit path for each version whose log ps-run-layer still owns. Add matrix rows for a version admitted at once while its log holds an earlier run's lines, and for a stop during wait-slots.

location: Boundaries > Always (Child: `--slot-cost n` stamps psm.slots on the PS container only); Ask First
issue: Only children started by ps-run-layer get --slot-cost. A direct `ps-e2e-run.py` run (SKILL.md Lapis 4, the e2e-quickstart TDD loop) boots a PS container with no psm.slots label, so the host-wide cap never counts it. The SPEC Constraints say the cap covers every running E2E container from every client of the daemon. The spec does not decide a default cost for direct runs or call the gap out. It also does not validate --slot-cost (0, negative, non-integer), does not say whether --run-id/--slot-cost/--progress-append are only valid together, and does not say what an unlabelled or malformed psm.slots value (for example 'x' or '0') counts as.
implementation_impact: The documented quickstart loop silently bypasses the cap and causes exactly the wait-healthy saturation that CAP-3 targets. A malformed label from another client can raise an exception inside the counting code, or be skipped and under-count.
suggestion: Decide explicitly: either direct E2E runs stamp psm.slots=1 by default (Layer 2/5 stay 0), or add the gap to Never/deferred-work with its rationale. Specify that --slot-cost must be an integer ≥ 1 (else exit 2), and that a non-integer or < 1 label value counts as the cap being full (or as 1). Add both cases to the Labels and Bad input rows.

issue: --slots is a per-invocation number that is checked against a daemon-wide sum. Two concurrent runs with different values (one with `--slots 1`, one with config 6) enforce different caps on the same daemon: the run with 6 admits while the sum is 5, and the run with 1 waits until it times out to no-slots. The docs task treats `--jobs` -> `--slots` as a rename. In run-phases.md, the advice to run one version per call with `--jobs 1` and the stall advice to 'turunkan --jobs' (lower --jobs) both have per-run meaning. Rewritten to `--slots 1`, they would make the operator's own run starve whenever any other E2E container exists anywhere on the daemon.
implementation_impact: Following the mechanically renamed docs produces spurious no-slots records. Two CAP-1 sessions with mismatched slot values can drive each other to blocked-infra.
suggestion: State in the docs task that --slots/psm_e2e_slots is a host-wide ceiling that every concurrent run should share. Replace the harness-without-background advice with 'one version per --cells call' (no --slots), and replace 'lower --jobs' with 'lower psm_e2e_slots in config for every session'. Optionally log a warning when a run's N differs from the psm.slots sum seen at admission.

location: Boundaries > Always ('--jobs with layer e2e = exit 2 naming --slots'); Code Map `main` (`--jobs`/`--slots`)
issue: ps-run-layer's argparse defines `--jobs` with `default=DEFAULT_JOBS` (3), so an explicit `--jobs` cannot be told apart from the default unless the default changes to None. The spec does not say this. It also does not say what happens with `--slots` or `--jobs` under `--merge-only --layer e2e` (the previous slice ignores `--jobs` there), or whether an invalid `psm_e2e_slots` in --config is an error for Layer 2/5 runs that never read it.
implementation_impact: A naive implementation rejects every e2e run, because args.jobs is always 3. Merge-only and Layer 2/5 config handling diverge between implementers, and the 'Bad input' row has no definitive expectation for these cases.
suggestion: Specify `--jobs` default=None, resolved to DEFAULT_JOBS for Layers 2/5. Under `--merge-only --layer e2e`, either --slots/--jobs → exit 2 or both are ignored (pick one). psm_e2e_slots is validated only for non-merge layer e2e. Add those rows to the matrix.

location: Tasks > ps-flashlight-run.py (`job_update(**fields)` rewriting the own registry entry); Design Notes > Claims
issue: Claims live in ps-run-layer's registry JSON, which other processes read while counting. The spec does not require atomic replacement (write a temp file, then rename). job_register's current write_text truncates the file and then writes it, and `_registry_entries` silently skips a file it cannot parse, so a reader that catches a half-written file drops that run's claims and over-admits. The spec also does not say whether claim removal after a reap takes slots.lock. When job_register fails to write the entry (OSError, entry_path None, today a silent pass), the run's claims are invisible to every other run, and the spec does not say whether that should abort the run or degrade it.
implementation_impact: There is an intermittent cap breach under concurrent runs that tests with stubs will never catch. A read-only or full /tmp turns the host-wide cap into a per-run cap with no signal to the operator.
suggestion: Require job_update and job_register to write a sibling temp file and os.replace it. Require claim add and remove under slots.lock. Make failure to persist a claim an exit 2 before any spawn (or a stderr warning plus fallback to admitting one cell at a time; pick one). Add a test where a corrupt or partial entry is present.

location: Tasks > tests ('harness stubs daemon_slot_usage, cleanup_orphans and points JOB_REGISTRY/lock dir at a temp dir'); Acceptance Criteria #2
issue: AC2 requires two ps-run-layer runs that share one registry, with a visible 'ALIVE wait-slots' line naming the claim. The existing harness runs ps-run-layer in-process with injected runners. Two in-process runs share the module-global `_JOB` (one entry_path), `RUN_ID`, OWNER_PID and `_PROGRESS`, so the second run's job_register/job_update overwrites the first run's entry bookkeeping. Running them as two processes means the stubs (daemon_slot_usage, cleanup_orphans) cannot be monkeypatched and need an env-var or file hook, which the spec does not define. ALIVE lines come every PROGRESS_HEARTBEAT (15 s), and the spec gives no injectable heartbeat or poll interval, so the test either sleeps for at least 15 s or cannot observe the line.
implementation_impact: AC2 is either untestable as specified or forces ad hoc test-only globals that the reviewer cannot check against the spec. The suite slows down by tens of seconds per wait-slots test.
suggestion: Specify the mechanism. Either the second 'run' is a real subprocess with stubs enabled through a documented test env var (for example PSM_TEST_SLOT_STUB=<json file>), or the AC is restated as a pre-seeded registry entry with a live claim (pid = test process) plus one in-process run. Make the heartbeat and admission poll intervals module constants that the tests override (for example 0.05 s).

location: Boundaries > Always (Slots: admission under slots.lock); Code Map ps-run-layer slot admission loop
issue: The spec does not give an admission poll interval, and it does not say whether slots.lock is held during the `docker ps` count, which can take up to DOCKER_CMD_TIMEOUT (120 s). If the lock is held across a slow or hung count, every ps-run-layer on the host blocks on the lock for up to 2 minutes per attempt. A blocking flock with no timeout also means a hung holder freezes every other run's admission, and that time is not counted toward their startup timeout. It also leaves undefined whether the ALIVE detail (counted containers and claims) is recomputed on every poll or frozen at the first attempt, even though AC2 expects the line to name the current claim.
implementation_impact: A slow daemon (the exact condition CAP-3 targets) serializes every run's admission behind one docker call, and wait-slots durations measure lock contention instead of slot availability.
suggestion: Specify a poll interval (for example 5 s). Under the lock, either take the docker snapshot with a short timeout, or take the snapshot outside the lock and re-validate it with only the registry read and the claim write inside. Acquire flock with a bounded retry so the wait counts toward wait-slots. Recompute the ALIVE detail on every poll.

location: Boundaries > Always (no-slots: 'counted containers (psm.job@host=cost) in errors'); Acceptance Criteria #2 ('ALIVE wait-slots lines naming the claim')
issue: The no-slots record and the ALIVE lines must list what fills the cap. The spec lists containers only, but live registry claims of other runs (whose containers are not running yet) also count, and the AC itself expects the claim to be named. For a failed docker count ('Count error' row), the spec does not say what goes into `errors`. The record could end up saying no-slots with an empty or misleading list and no docker error text.
implementation_impact: The operator cannot tell which foreign job to clean or stop. Contract Config keys says the list exists precisely so that a foreign orphan can be cleaned from its owner. The Count-error case is undiagnosable.
suggestion: Define the errors/ALIVE payload as containers `psm.job@host=cost` plus claims `claim:<run>@<job>=cost`. When the count fails, use the docker error text (truncated) and 'count failed: treated as full'. Assert both in the Foreign full and Count error rows.

location: Design Notes > Interim cost/mode; Never section
issue: Every version runs with --sequential-browsers and no snapshot-db reset, but its records still carry `browser_mode: sequential`. The contract (Parallel browsers > Slots) defines sequential mode as resetting to a snapshot before each later engine. Records made in this slice are gate-grade and stay fresh until the source changes, so after CAP-7 lands they are indistinguishable from contract-conformant sequential evidence even though Firefox ran on a DB that Chromium had already mutated.
implementation_impact: The honesty guarantee that 'each engine starts from the same state' is silently claimed by evidence that does not meet it. A residue-masked Firefox pass from this slice could satisfy `ready` after CAP-7 without a rerun.
suggestion: Either stamp a marker (for example `browser_mode: sequential-shared-db`, or a note in `browser_notes`) that later readers treat as non-gate-grade once CAP-7 lands, or record in deferred-work that CAP-7 must stale pre-CAP-7 sequential records (for example via an evidence schema version in the fingerprint comparison).

location: Tasks > docs (SKILL.md, run-phases.md, headless.md, README only); context companion spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.interim-orchestration.md
issue: After this slice, a multi-version `--cells` run stops at the first fail and appends not-run records. The approved interim orchestration companion still says '--jobs as today' (Fase 2 step 3), which now exits 2. Its 'Run outcomes' classification knows only fail / inconclusive / inconclusive-steps / browser-notes, so the plan reason `not-run` has no defined handling. 'V's E2E step is due' is keyed on 'an E2E run of V printed the current source_fingerprint', which a run that left V not-run arguably satisfies, so V is never retried in the session. Headless callers (psm-develop, psm-cross-version, psm-optimize) lose per-version verdicts for not-run versions, and the CAP-1 `reached`/'not reached' handling that the contract uses to explain this is deferred. The docs task does not cover any of this.
implementation_impact: The orchestrator either calls ps-run-layer with --jobs (exit 2, treated as a pre-spawn input error loop), or treats not-run versions as neither failed nor infra and stalls or reports them inconsistently. psm-optimize can misreport a not-run version as 'no new failure'.
suggestion: Add a docs/companion task. Update the interim orchestration (or its successor text in run-phases.md/headless.md) to (a) use --slots, (b) classify reason `not-run` as 'not attempted: due again', with no-slots as an infra reason, and (c) exclude not-run cells from the 'printed the fingerprint' test. Tell headless callers that a version whose cells are all not-run is unproven, never a pass or a per-version finding.

location: Boundaries > Always (Child: `--sequential-browsers` engine fail-fast; 'ps-run-layer copies a child-emitted not-run cell into the record as is')
issue: 'As is' conflicts with the existing build_record path. Today every cell that has child data goes through derive_state, which turns a never-driven cell into `inconclusive/not-driven`. The spec does not say which fields ps-run-layer still fills or overrides for such a cell (started_at/finished_at null -> admission/write time, phase_durations with merged wait-slots, session, fingerprint, job_id, image_tag). It also does not say which state the child uses to decide 'fail' in the middle of the loop. If the child judges fail from findings alone, while version-level errors or install would make ps-run-layer's merged record inconclusive, then firefox ends up not-run 'after 9.1:chromium' while the chromium record is not a fail, and the run-level trigger never fires.
implementation_impact: Records can name a trigger cell whose own record is not `fail`, which breaks the not-run invariant in cell-contract.md and confuses the plan's focus-cell logic in CAP-1.
suggestion: Specify that the child decides an engine's fail with cell_state (the same derive_state over the merged version-level errors/install). Specify that ps-run-layer skips derive_state only for cells with `state: not-run` and a reason matching `^fail-fast after `, keeps their state, conclusive and reason, and fills the run-level fields and timestamps as for any record without an engine. Add a test where a not-run cell from the child round-trips into history unchanged except for those fields.
